judgment.notes: At S003, M003 is instantiated with A=ℂ, T=V, Q the subtype of integers in I, and f=e. The field and complex module structures come from the declared representation. S001/F001 gives finite cardinal λ+1>0, hence nonemptiness (also 0∈I). S002/F002 supplies independence. H004's complex dimension λ+1 is finrank over ℂ, equal to card(I) by F001 and D001. Its conclusion is exactly span(range e)=V; combined with independence this licenses the basis and finite coefficient expansions used in S003. BG001 separately checks the routine binomial identity with natural arguments λ-i,r and i,r; all are nonnegative in their respective branches. No E application occurs.

S001's simultaneous induction follows by the representation commutator identities; the x step coefficient m(λ-m+1)+λ-2m=(m+1)(λ-m) is correct, including m=0 separately. S002 iterates the x identity to obtain a nonzero multiple of v for each i≤λ; factorials are nonzero complex scalars. Its isolating polynomial kills every other eigenvector and multiplies e_j by the nonzero product ∏_{k≠j}2(k-j), proving independence without importing an eigenvector-independence theorem. S003 correctly applies M003 and uses that independence on the expansion of y^{λ+1}v: h+ (λ+2)Id multiplies the i-coordinate by 2(λ+1-i)≠0. Thus the vector is zero, and every higher power is zero. S004's factorial normalization gives the stated x,y,h coefficients; repeated actions give the displayed rising products, and crossing e_0 or the terminating highest index gives exactly the two zero branches. BG001 verifies conversion of those products to integral binomial coefficients. For r=0 the products are empty and both divided powers are identities; λ=0 also satisfies every endpoint formula.

Every direct input has an actual role: H003 gives λ≥0 and positive interval size; H004 gives the commutators, complex module structure and dimension; H005 supplies the induction base and v≠0; M003 supplies spanning from the proved independence and cardinal/dimension equality. The upper bound λ<p, irreducibility itself, and [h,x]=2x are not needed in this inference, but their hypotheses remain intact. The core independence and termination arguments are displayed locally, not imported as named theorems. BG001 accounts for the omitted routine rising-factorial/binomial identity and integrality; no project lemma or additional hypothesis is added.
